package_info.package_manager: kernel source (not a package manager, but distributed via Linux distributions)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected Linux kernel versions contain a vulnerability (Dirty Pipe, CVE-2022-0847) that allows unprivileged users to write arbitrary data to any file they can read, enabling privilege escalation and container escape. Exploitation code leverages this flaw to overwrite critical system files or binaries, resulting in full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (local exploit execution by unprivileged user)
execution_context.file_location: user-supplied exploit code (typically a C program or PoC script run on the vulnerable system)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses the splice system call to manipulate the Linux kernel page cache, allowing arbitrary data to be written to a file (e.g., /etc/passwd) that the user can only read, resulting in privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unprivileged users should not be able to write to files like /etc/passwd, which are critical for system security. The use of splice with PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE to bypass normal write restrictions is highly abnormal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only privileged users (root) can modify /etc/passwd or other protected files. This exploit allows unprivileged users to do so.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: The splice syscall is legitimately used for efficient data transfer between file descriptors, but not for modifying protected files.
key_indicators: splice system call used on non-world-writable files
attempts to write to /etc/passwd or other critical system files

execution_context.trigger: runtime (local exploit execution from within a container)
execution_context.file_location: user-supplied exploit code (run inside a container)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses the splice system call to overwrite the RunC binary from within a container, enabling the attacker to execute arbitrary code on the host and escape the container.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Containerized processes should not be able to modify host binaries. Overwriting RunC from a container is a clear sign of a container escape attempt.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Containers are expected to be isolated from the host and not able to alter host binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate scenario exists for a container process to overwrite the host's RunC binary.
key_indicators: splice system call targeting executable files in /usr/bin or similar paths
modification of container runtime binaries from within a container

execution_context.file_location: user-supplied exploit code (targeting any critical system file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses the splice system call to overwrite files in critical system paths (e.g., /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin), potentially replacing system binaries with malicious payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overwriting system binaries by unprivileged users is a clear privilege escalation and persistence technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only privileged users should be able to modify system binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System updates or package installations by root may legitimately overwrite these files, but not by unprivileged users.
key_indicators: splice system call on files in /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, etc.
modification of executable files by non-root users

attack_chain.action: Attacker runs exploit code as an unprivileged user or from within a container.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary write to files readable by the attacker (e.g., /etc/passwd, /usr/bin/runc, system binaries).

attack_chain.action: Exploit code uses splice syscall with PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE to overwrite target file contents.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation (e.g., new root user in /etc/passwd) or container escape (overwriting RunC).

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains elevated privileges or escapes container, achieving full system or host compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: root access or host takeover.

behavioral_signatures: splice system call used on files that are not world-writable
modification of critical system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, /bin/*, /usr/bin/runc) by unprivileged users
file_indicators: executables in /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/local/sbin, /boot modified by non-root users
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the splice system call being used by unprivileged users on files that are not world-writable, especially when the PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE flag is set. Alert on any attempts to modify critical system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, system binaries) by non-root users. Use eBPF or audit frameworks to track these syscall patterns in real time.
